Article Title: Satya Nadella has a new 'headache', Microsoft's 'breakup' with Disney, as Mouse House dumps ...
Article Text:
Copilot’s Struggles



Disney’s AI favourites



Microsoft’s revamp efforts



Why Microsoft is asking Google and Amazon for 'help' despite spending $190 billion on AI



Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has a fresh challenge on his hands: Disney is dropping GitHub Copilot and several other AI coding tools in the US starting Augurs, according to an internal message viewed by Business Insider. This move of the company does not apply internationally, but it marks a significant setback for Microsoft’s AI product suite. Disney is now preparing to adopt OpenAI’s Codex as its coding assistant, while retaining access to Anthropic’s Claude Enterprise and Cursor. At the same time, Disney revealed that it will drop two Amazon tools which include the agentic code editor Kiro and AI assistant Q. Claude will also no longer be accessible through Amazon Web Services Bedrock.Eight Disney tech employees told Business Insider they rarely or never used GitHub Copilot. One product manager said Copilot produced “needlessly complex” code requiring clean-up, while a longtime engineer said their access had “lapsed for lack of use.” The frustration was compounded last month when Microsoft shifted Copilot’s pricing to a token-based model, sparking backlash even as executives claimed it fuelled GitHub’s “best month ever.Claude and Cursor have become fan favourites among Disney engineers. Some superusers reportedly invoke these tools tens of thousands of times per day, with one high-level engineer estimating that 80% of their coding at the terminal is done with Claude. Disney’s streaming leaders even created an AI adoption dashboard to track usage, encouraging staff to boost velocity and output.Microsoft has been working to revamp GitHub and shake up its Copilot teams to better compete with rivals OpenAI and Anthropic. But Disney’s decision underscores the uphill battle Nadella faces as Copilot struggles to gain traction in a market increasingly dominated by more popular AI coding assistants.Microsoft is spending a record $190 billion to build AI infrastructure, and it is still short enough on servers that it has started evaluating Amazon and Google—its two biggest cloud rivals—as suppliers.According to a Business Insider report, the company is now evaluating Amazon and Google as sources of additional cloud capacity, with one person familiar with the discussions putting it plainly: "We are shopping for capacity everywhere." Amazon has already stepped in once, bailing Microsoft out following a series of GitHub outages this year. Microsoft also explored leasing infrastructure from Oracle but walked away over security and compliance concerns. For a company whose Azure pitch rests on owning the stack end to end, that is an uncomfortable place to be.
Article Summary: Disney is dropping GitHub Copilot and several other AI coding tools in the US starting Augurs. This move of the company does not apply internationally, but it marks a significant setback for Microsoft's AI product suite. Disney is now preparing to adopt OpenAI’s Codex as its coding assistant. At the same time, Disney revealed that it will drop two Amazon tools.

Article Title: Less than a week after Thinking Machines cofounder Lilian Weng resigned citing stress and illness, she is rejoining Sam Altman
Article Text:
Health challenges among AI leaders



Less than a week after announcing her resignation from Thinking Machines Lab citing stress and illness, cofounder Lilian Weng is now returning to work alongside OpenAI CEO Sam Altman . According to a report by Business Insider, Weng, who previously served as OpenAI’s vice president of research and safety, said she had been ill more often in the past seven months than at any other point in her life. In her farewell post, she explained that the “consistent stress and workload” of building a startup had pushed her beyond what her health could sustain.Weng’s departure came as Thinking Machines was sprinting to release its first open-weight model, Inkling. She admitted feeling “guilt” about taking sick leave during that critical period and considered narrowing her role before deciding to step away entirely. “If I cannot give it 100% for what I should be responsible for, I fail my job,” she wrote. But just days later, Weng has chosen to rejoin Altman in a scoped role that promises more predictability and less strain than her cofounder responsibilities. A report by TechCrunch revealed that OpenAI has confirmed that Weng will be joining the company as the VP of AI Safety Research.“I've always been a curiosity-driven person. Leaning new knowledge or figuring out how to solve problems that are not well defined often gives me simple joy.The fun part of being a cofounder is how it "forced" me to develop new perspectives on company strategies, team building (at the company level), and much more, as well as how these seemingly abstract terms are deeply connected with our day-to-day actions, planning and narratives. With real-world experience, ideas that once felt theoretical become approachable and it is true for many terms in many domains,” wrote Weng in a post on X.Mira Murati the founder of Thinking Machines Lab thanked Weng for everything. “We’ll miss you, it’s been wonderful building Thinky together. I’m glad that you’re putting your health first. Thank you for everything.”Her move follows a string of health-related step-backs across the AI industry. Earlier this month, Fidji Simo left her full-time role as OpenAI’s CEO of AGI after a flare-up of POTS, while Greg Yang of xAI shifted into an advisory role after being diagnosed with Lyme disease. The pressures of leading frontier AI labs have increasingly highlighted the toll on executives’ health.Thinking Machines itself has been hit hard by Silicon Valley’s AI talent war. A Business Insider review found that 13 of its 42 founding members have left since launch, including three of its six cofounders, as rivals like Meta and OpenAI offered lucrative compensation packages. Weng’s return to Altman underscores how talent continues to circulate among the most influential players in AI.
Article Summary: Lilian Weng, cofounder of Thinking Machines Lab, announced her resignation last week. Weng said she had been ill more often in the past seven months than at any other point in her life. In her farewell post, she explained that the “consistent stress and workload” had pushed her beyond what her health could sustain.

Article Title: Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary predicts that America, Canada and Mexico will unite due to the fear of rise of ...
Article Text:
The rising Chinese competition



One of 'biggest AI problems' is forcing American and European companies to use Chinese models



Canadian billionaire and former Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary feels that fear of China’s rise will be the driving force behind deeper economic integration between the United States, Canada and Mexico. According to a report by Business Insider, O’Leary posted a video on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) in which the venture capitalist said that covers over China’s advances in AI, technology, warfare and power generation will outweigh political disagreements across North America. O’Leary argued that each country brings unique strengths to the table: “Canada has the energy and critical minerals, the United States has the scale and innovation, and Mexico plays a vital role in the North American economy,” he said. He added that cooperation is not just good policy but “an economic necessity” as the race for AI, energy, and critical infrastructure accelerates.The made by O’Leary come amid the growing recognition of China’s technological momentum. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk also recently told Economist that China already produces far more electricity than the US and it could become the world’s AI leader if it manages to secure enough computing power.American AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic have also warned that Chinese rivals are closing the gap, with Beijing-based Moonshot AI drawing attention for its Kimi K3 model.Automobile executives including Ford CEO Jim Farley, Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe, and Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi have repeatedly highlighted Chinese automakers’ dominance in electric vehicle production. Despite this, North America remains fragmented, with President Donald Trump recently imposing 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods.Recently, it was revealed that the cost of running sophisticated AI is pushing companies away from American labs toward China, a report has said, claiming that businesses ranging from Silicon Valley startups to European industrial giants are quietly replacing top-tier US AI models with cheaper Chinese alternatives, and integrating them into their business operations.A report by The Financial Times claims that household brands like DoorDash, Airbnb and German engineering giant Siemens have all adopted AI tools built in China. The mass migration is being fueled by a corporate race to solve the industry’s biggest headache: the ballooning cost of using AI caused by a sudden shift from flat-rate subscriptions to usage-based billing.Faced with massive bills, companies appear to have realised they no longer need the absolute most advanced and expensive model to handle everyday business routines. Chinese models from groups like DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Z.ai have rapidly overtaken their US rivals in text and data processing efficiency, the report claims.
Article Summary: Venture capitalist Kevin O’Leary says fear of China’s rise will be the driving force behind deeper economic integration between the U.S., Canada and Mexico. He said cooperation is not just good policy but “an economic necessity” as the race for AI, energy, and critical infrastructure accelerates.

Article Title: Rogue AI agent of Sam Altman's OpenAI hacked more than one multi-billion company, a New York-based CTO makes new revelations
Article Text:
Sam Altman

Unauthenticated code exploited on Modal’s infrastructure



OpenAI confirms breach across multiple services



The rogue OpenAI agent that executed a high-profile cyberattack on world’s biggest AI model repository, Hugging Face, also breached systems hosted by cloud startup Modal Labs, essentially extending its reach further than previously revealed. The new details, published by Hugging Face and reported by news agency Reuters, reveal that the experimental AI agent reached additional customer systems during its multi-day breakout earlier this month.The incident has now intensified concerns over the safety and containment of autonomous AI systems as developers test their capabilities even as several AI giants have come together to pledge a coordinated effort to develop and share tools for AI safety and cybersecurity.According to a timeline released by Hugging Face, the autonomous AI agent initially broke out of its sandbox, which is essentially an isolated testing space, hosted on a third-party provider’s infrastructure. The agent then used that breach as a launching pad for a broader platform-level attack on Hugging Face.Akshat Bubna, CTO of New York-based Modal Labs, confirmed that Modal was the third-party provider involved.However, Bubna emphasized that the breach stemmed from insecure code published by a customer, rather than a security flaw in Modal's core architecture.“Modal's platform or isolation were not compromised in any way,” Bubna told Reuters, explaining that the customer had “published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution”.While OpenAI declined to comment directly on Modal’s statements, the company pointed to an updated disclosure confirming that its agent accessed four accounts across four separate third-party services.OpenAI stated that while the agent accessed multiple accounts, it found “no other activity at the level of severity or scale of what we've shared related to Hugging Face, which involved a platform-level compromise”.
Article Summary: The rogue OpenAI agent that executed a high-profile cyberattack on world’s biggest AI model repository, Hugging Face, also breached systems hosted by cloud startup Modal Labs. New details reveal that the experimental AI agent reached additional customer systems during its multi-day breakout earlier this month.

Article Title: Canada's Brookfield partners America's largest electric company to turn former nuclear weapons facility into $100 billion data centre and 'reason' is Silicon Valley’s 'promise'
Article Text:
Flag of Canada

Silicon Valley's 'electricity promise' to White House



Brookfield and NextEra Energy are reportedly planning a $100 billion data centre and energy complex at a former uranium enrichment site in Kentucky, as investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure accelerates across the United States. According to a report in the Financial Times, Canada's Brookfield is teaming up with the US’s largest electric utility to build a massive data centre and energy complex on a former nuclear enrichment facility that played an important role in America’s nuclear weapons programme during the cold war.The project in Paducah, western Kentucky, will include 2 gigawatts of natural gas-fired generation and 2.6 gigawatts of battery storage. The planned gas plants would have enough generating capacity to supply about 1.5 million homes.The US Department of Energy has agreed to lease more than 3,500 acres at the government-owned site, where uranium enrichment operations ended in 2013, according to a person familiar with the matter cited in the report. The facility played an important role in the US nuclear weapons programme during the Cold War. The privately financed campus is expected to begin operating in phases from 2028 and be completed by early 2032.Brookfield has begun discussions with major cloud computing companies about becoming anchor tenants at the site, according to a person close to the project. Brookfield chief executive Bruce Flatt reportedly said the development would serve as the starting point for the investment group’s plan to deploy $100 billion in AI infrastructure. “By advancing this project in line with the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge, we are ensuring innovation and affordability go hand in hand while creating high-quality jobs, attracting new investment and strengthening the local economy,” Flatt said, as per the report.Earlier this month, US President Donald Trump announced that about 200 entities have signed on to his non-binding “Ratepayer Protection Pledge”, expanding a voluntary commitment which claims to ensure US consumers will not bear the cost of the AI datacenter build-out. The pledge, first announced in March this year, was initially signed by seven tech companies: Google, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, xAI, OpenAI and Amazon. It will now cover companies delivering 80% of all power to US homes and businesses, according to the White House.“Electricity rates for 80% of the power distributed in America are now being kept in check by the plan,” Trump said at a press conference. Trump added that “radical left communists” are the ones who “want to shut down all new development, kill our most successful industries, destroy hundreds of thousands of jobs, and surrender the AI race to China”.Pledge comes at a time when more than a dozen states have considered moratoria on datacenters, and New York became the first US state to enact a temporary ban this month. Senator Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a representative, have also proposed a national moratorium.
Article Summary: Brookfield and NextEra Energy are reportedly planning a $100 billion data centre and energy complex at a former uranium enrichment site in Kentucky. The project in Paducah, western Kentucky, will include 2 gigawatts of natural gas-fired generation and 2.6 Gigawatts of battery storage. The planned gas plants would have enough generating capacity to supply about 1.5 million homes.

Article Title: US government continues ban on Chinese technology, now bans the gadgets that Elon Musk once said are Tesla's biggest competition
Article Text:
During Tesla earnings call, Elon Musk said “I think China will be by far the biggest competitor in the humanoid robot market" (Representative image)

What US government said on banning China’s humanoid robots

When Elon Musk called China’s humanoid robots as Tesla’s biggest long-term competition





The US Federal Communications Commission has banned humanoid robots from China citing "unacceptable risks” to national security. The Trump administration identified human robots as advanced robotic devices that include four-legged quadrupeds, bipeds, and wheeled and tracked vehicles. The move comes as the US government continues to tighten its control on Chinese technology across sectors ranging from telecommunications and drones to artificial intelligence to now humanoid robots. Notably, Elon Musk has previously described China’s humanoid robots as Tesla’s biggest long-term competition.In its determination of the threats posed by robots, FCC said:“As the technology matures, advanced robotic devices have growing use cases in monitoring and securing critical infrastructure. Robots are often equipped with high-fidelity sensors, including Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), tactile, acoustic, and thermal sensors that collect and maintain sensitive data on their surroundings”.“In addition to securing critical infrastructure, advanced robotic devices also have applications in industrial manufacturing, from material handling to order fulfilment. Integrating these technologies into American manufacturing will lower production costs, increase output, and support America’s reindustrialization.In order for the American economy to rely on these technologies, we must have a secure domestic advanced robotics supply chain and industrial Base,” it further stated.Adding further, the FCC said:“All foreign-produced advanced robotic devices pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States and to the safety and security of U.S. persons and should be included on the FCC’s Covered List, unless the Department of War (DOW) transmits to the FCC a specific determination that a given foreign-produced advanced robotic device, or a class of such devices, does not pose such risks”.Speaking at the company’s earnings call recently, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said that the electric vehicle maker’s future is increasingly tied to Optimus, humanoid robot program. "My prediction is that Optimus will be the biggest product of all time by far," Elon Musk said on the call. "Nothing will even be close. I think it'll be ten times bigger than the next biggest product ever made. That level," he added.During the earnings, he also acknowledged that Tesla is unlikely to dominate it alone. “I think China will be by far the biggest competitor in the humanoid robot market,” he said adding “China is extremely good at scaling and manufacturing, and is also strong in AI — the models being released there are already quite good and are improving rapidly.”“China's very good at AI, very good at manufacturing, and will definitely be the toughest competition for Tesla,” Elon Musk said, adding “To the best of our knowledge, we don't see any significant competitors outside of China, but China will definitely be tough competition, there's no two ways about it.”
Article Summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has banned humanoid robots from China citing ‘unacceptable risks’ to national security. The move comes as the US government continues to tighten its control on Chinese technology across sectors ranging from telecommunications and drones to artificial intelligence. Notably, Elon Musk has previously described China’s humanoid robots as Tesla's biggest long-term competition.

Article Title: Apple touches $5 trillion market cap and one of the reasons is what has made Wall Street ‘unhappy’ with Google, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon
Article Text:
Why Alphabet’s capex hike changed how investors read AI spending across Big Tech



How Apple’s rented AI infrastructure keeps its cash flow intact while rivals borrow



Apple shares hit $342.89 on Tuesday, briefly putting the company’s market value at $5.036 trillion. That makes it the second company ever to reach $5 trillion, after Nvidia. The stock closed at $340.08, so the milestone lasted only part of the session. On Monday, Apple had already passed Nvidia to become the world’s most valuable public company again.Apple’s capital expenditure in fiscal 2025 was $12.7 billion. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta will spend more than $700 billion between them this year, nearly all of it on AI data centres. Twelve months ago that gap was Apple’s biggest problem on Wall Street. It is now the reason investors are buying the stock, and the shift happened almost entirely in the last week.Alphabet raised the top end of its 2026 capex forecast to $205 billion from $190 billion last Wednesday. Its cloud business grew 82% in the quarter, the fastest since at least 2020. The stock still fell 7% the next day, and took Amazon, Meta and Microsoft down with it.What spooked investors was the debt. Alphabet’s long-term borrowings have risen 111% to $98 billion in six months, and the company posted negative free cash flow last quarter for the first time.Amazon’s long-term debt climbed 81% to $119 billion between December and March. FactSet’s analysts now expect Microsoft’s free cash flow to turn negative in the fourth quarter, which would be a first since at least 2001.Apple buys compute rather than building it. CFO Kevan Parekh has called it a hybrid model, mixing first and third-party capacity, with Apple silicon running the servers it does own. The Siri overhaul due this fall leans on Google’s AI technology.The result showed up in March: over $28 billion in operating cash flow, capex under $3 billion, almost all of it free cash. “Once criticized for not spending more on AI, they have been able to avoid some of those capex pitfalls,” said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets. Apple is up about 25% this year. Nvidia, which crossed $5 trillion in October, has managed 6%.Microsoft and Meta report Wednesday after the close, Amazon on Thursday. All three are expected to raise spending guidance. Cowen analyst Derrick Wood said another increase would probably trigger more selling.Apple reports Thursday evening, with analysts forecasting revenue growth above 15%. It will be Tim Cook’s last earnings call. John Ternus takes over on September 1.
Article Summary: Apple shares hit $342.89 on Tuesday, briefly putting the company’s market value at $5.036 trillion. That makes it the second company ever to reach $5 trillion, after Nvidia. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta will spend more than $700 billion between them this year.

Article Title: Two solar farms in Minnesota restored native wildflowers and proved beneficial for bees, butterflies proving to scientists what everyone got wrong
Article Text:
Representative Image

How native vegetation helped pollinators recover

Why the findings matter

Solar farms and ecosystem restoration

Two solar farms in Minnesota have reportedly helped restore local ecosystems. According to a study by researchers at Argonne National Laboratory, the solar farms have restored native wildflowers and grasses while increasing populations of beneficial insects. The findings add what scientists describe as evidence that solar farms can contribute to habitat restoration and pollinator conservation when developed with native vegetation.After monitoring the two sites for five years, researchers found significant increases in native plants as well as in insects, including bees, butterflies, wasps, and hornets. Bee populations increased about 20-fold, while the overall number of beneficial insects tripled compared with earlier observations.The two solar farms were developed on retired agricultural land and replanted with native wildflowers and grasses. Researchers tracked changes in vegetation and insect populations over five years to assess how the sites affected local biodiversity.The study found that restoring native plant species created habitats that supported pollinating insects, with bees showing the largest increase. Butterflies, wasps and hornets also became more abundant as native vegetation became established.Researchers said the results are significant because expanding renewable energy infrastructure will require large areas of land. Estimates suggest that meeting future solar energy demand could require around 10 million acres for solar development.Using retired farmland and restoring it with native vegetation could reduce ecological impacts while creating habitats for pollinators. According to the researchers, insects supported by the solar farms also moved into nearby agricultural areas, where they helped pollinate crops.The findings come as insect populations continue to decline in many regions due to factors such as climate change and pesticide use. Beetles, bees, butterflies and other insects help pollinate crops and sustain healthy ecosystems. Other insects help sustain soil health and biodiversity.The Minnesota study shows that solar projects paired with native habitat restoration can not only generate renewable electricity, but also benefit local ecosystems and boost pollinator numbers.
Article Summary: Two solar farms in Minnesota have reportedly helped restore local ecosystems. Researchers tracked changes in vegetation and insect populations over five years to assess how the sites affected local biodiversity. Bee populations increased about 20-fold, while the overall number of beneficial insects tripled compared with earlier observations.

Article Title: Quote of the Day by Julie Sweet: ‘I have an unwavering commitment to inclusion and diversity’
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Julie Sweet

Quote of the day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet



"I have an unwavering commitment to

inclusion and diversity

."

What Julie Sweet's quote means

A message tested by real events



Julie Sweet has led Accenture, one of the world's largest professional services companies with roughly 770,000 employees across more than 120 countries, since 2019. A few themes have run through her public statements but one stands out and none of them is as consistently as this one. Unlike a lot of corporate language on the subject, which tends to stay vague and aspirational, Sweet has repeated this stance across interviews and reports for close to a decade. That repetition is itself part of the message: a position she keeps restating on the record.The word doing the heavy lifting here is “unwavering”. The quote adjusts a goal, a target and a program with a fixed personal position, framed as something that doesn't move regardless of business conditions, market pressure or the broader corporate climate. That's a stronger claim than most companies make about their own values, and it's also a harder one to walk back gracefully, which matters, given what's happened since.There’s also a shift worth noticing in how the sentence is built. Sweet says “I,” not “Accenture” or “we.” Most corporate diversity language is written to sound institutional and permanent. But Sweet's phrasing puts her own name behind it, tying her personal credibility to the outcome rather than hiding behind the company's.Sweet has used language like this publicly not long after taking over as CEO, and repeated it consistently through the years that followed, including in Accenture's Fiscal 2024 Annual Report, published in October 2024. Less than four months later, in February 2025, Sweet told employees in an internal memo that Accenture was ending several of its DEI-specific goals and programs, including its long-standing target of a gender-balanced global workforce by 2025 — a target the company had held since 2017.Around the same time, Accenture renamed its public-facing DEI webpage from “Our commitment to inclusion & diversity” to “Everyone is welcome here.” Accenture’s own framing of the shift was that the underlying commitment to a workplace where everyone belongs hadn't changed, even as the specific representation targets and named programs built around it were retired.Critics saw it differently, pointing to the gap between the language used just months earlier and the programs that were subsequently wound down. Either way, the episode is a real-world test of how durable a CEO's stated values turn out to be once external pressure – in this case, a broader US corporate retreat from DEI commitments through 2024 and 2025 – enters the picture.
Article Summary: Julie Sweet has led Accenture, one of the world's largest professional services companies, since 2019. The quote adjusts a goal, a target and a program with a fixed personal position. It's a stronger claim than most companies make about their own values.

Article Title: Apple’s incoming CEO John Ternus says company will expand entertainment business
Article Text:
Apple to focus on ‘quality over quantity’ strategy



Apple to leverage hardware and unique partnerships



Apple’s incoming CEO, hardware chief John Ternus, has committed to expanding the tech giant’s entertainment footprint when he officially takes the helm of the iPhone maker in September. Speaking on the red carpet at the fourth season premiere of “Ted Lasso” this week, Ternus highlighted the company's streaming trajectory alongside outgoing CEO Tim Cook, news agency Reuters reported.“I think we have such tremendous momentum right now in Apple TV. There's so many amazing shows, so many amazing characters and stories, and so we're just going to keep building on the momentum," Ternus told Reuters.Apple first launched its original TV series and films through Apple TV+ in 2019, securing major hits including the Oscar-winning film “CODA,” the box-office success “F1”, and acclaimed series such as “The Studio” and “Ted Lasso”. Last year, the company rebranded the service by dropping the ‘plus’ sign, renaming it simply Apple TV.Meanwhile, Cook noted that he is actively sharing insights about the entertainment industry as part of the leadership transition. Cook reiterated that Apple’s core strategy will remain focused on prestige content rather than volume.“Our role is to be the best. That's our lane. We're not about the most. There are...other companies that do that. But we're about the best, and I feel like we really hit our stride in providing that,” Cook explained.Cook highlighted that Apple remains open to future media partnerships, provided the company can bring unique technological innovations to the deal. He cited Apple’s broad partnership with Formula 1 as a prime model.Apple engineered custom camera systems for the Brad Pitt feature film “F1” to capture immersive racing footage while during the same time, F1 races started streaming exclusively on Apple TV in the US. Apple provides real-time leaderboards, updates and race coverage integrated directly into Apple News and companion apps.“We'll do things that we can bring something unique to, where we can innovate in a way that others might not be able to. I feel like we're really doing that with F1. We're so excited about how we're doing there and the viewership numbers that we're getting. So more things like that would be possible,” Cook said.The executive transition comes shortly after senior Apple executive Eddy Cue signaled that the company aims to deliver “better and more” films and TV shows across both streaming platforms and traditional cinemas in the coming years.
Article Summary: incoming CEO John Ternus committed to expanding the tech giant’s entertainment footprint when he officially takes the helm in September. Apple first launched its original TV series and films through Apple TV+ in 2019, securing major hits including the Oscar-winning film “CODA,” the box-office success “F1”, and acclaimed series such as “The Studio” and “Ted Lasso”

Article Title: Quote of the day by Steve Jobs: “The only way to do great work is to love what you do. If you haven't found it yet, keep…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Steve Jobs



“The only way to do great work is to love what you do. If you haven't found it yet, keep looking. Don't settle.”

What is the meaning behind Steve Jobs ’ famous words



How curiosity shaped Steve Jobs’ path to Apple



Steve Jobs and the pursuit of meaningful work



What the quote reveals about persistence



The difference between passion and perfection



Lessons from Jobs’ approach to work



Curiosity can guide direction. Exploring different interests can reveal opportunities that were not obvious at the beginning.

Setbacks do not always define the outcome. Jobs’ career included failures that later became part of his experience.

Meaning matters alongside success. Achievements can feel different when they are connected to something a person values.

Growth requires movement. Staying open to change can help people discover new possibilities.

A reminder not to settle too quickly



The process of finding meaning in one's work is something that most people encounter in their life at different stages. While success can be defined by way of accomplishment, recognition, or monetary gain, the motivation behind the work itself should not be overlooked. The quest for fulfilling work is about discovering one's interests, acquiring knowledge and skills, growing through obstacles and experiences, and being ready to find new opportunities. A person's career doesn't usually go according to any plans, and many people find their passions by exploring.The notion of doing what you love is an embodiment of devotion, curiosity, and creativity. It helps to remember that great things take time to achieve.Steve Jobs shared this idea during his 2005 commencement speech at Stanford University, where he spoke about connecting experiences, dealing with setbacks, and making choices based on personal conviction. Though the quote may be considered an encouragement to follow one’s passion, its meaning is far from being simple. Jobs did not encourage people to live their lives with the impression that each day at work will bring excitement and fun.Jobs’ life and career had its ups and downs; he faced difficulties, controversies, doubts and even opposition to his ideas.While finding something you love might sound like an idea that each person has only one passion in life which needs to be found, in practice, people usually cultivate their interests as well. Different skills are acquired, experiences change perceptions, and career development might be full of surprises.Indeed, Steve Jobs had his own unconventional route. He left college and tried different disciplines, he took classes because of their attraction despite not knowing where exactly they would lead him. Interest in design, technology, and simplicity helped to create Apple’s products philosophy.Steve Jobs co-founded Apple Inc. in 1976 alongside Steve Wozniak and helped transform the way people interacted with personal technology. Under his leadership, Apple introduced products that focused heavily on design, user experience, and simplicity.His career also included difficult moments. He was removed from Apple in 1985 after internal disagreements and spent years away from the company he helped create. During that period, he founded NeXT and became involved with Pixar Animation Studios.When Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, the company was struggling. His second period at the organisation led to the development of products such as the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, which changed the technology industry.His career was not built on avoiding failure. It was shaped by continuing to work on ideas he believed mattered.The phrase “keep looking” means as much as being passionate about one’s job. This is due to the understanding that many people devote several years to experimenting with various positions, industries and types of creativity until they find something that suits them.This message of Jobs was intended for those who are unsure about their ways. Being in the position that is somehow disconnected even because it looks like a safe option can cause frustration for many years. The message suggested people keep on searching instead of taking an unsatisfactory path.However, it is important to note that the quote does not imply that every hard time a person goes through is an indicator of choosing the wrong career. Every profession is connected with routine things and moments of struggle and frustration. Sometimes, passion about the overall idea of what one does may be more important than about everything else.A common misunderstanding around Jobs’ statement is that passion should always come first. For many people, passion develops after gaining experience and becoming skilled at something. A person may not begin a career feeling deeply connected to their work. Confidence, expertise, and familiarity can gradually create a stronger relationship with a profession. Enjoyment sometimes follows improvement rather than causing it.Jobs himself was known for his attention to detail and high expectations. His approach involved constant refinement and questioning whether products could be made better. Loving the work, in his view, was closely connected with caring about the final result.The quote offers several ideas that extend beyond career decisions:Steve Jobs’ words are often treated as a statement about ambition, but they also contain an element of patience. Finding fulfilling work is rarely an immediate process. It involves trying, adjusting, learning, and sometimes starting again.The idea behind “don’t settle” is not necessarily about chasing a perfect career. It is about remaining engaged with the search and recognising when something no longer reflects what a person wants to build.For Jobs, great work came from a strong connection between effort and purpose. His quote continues to be remembered because it speaks to a question that extends beyond any single profession: how do people create work they genuinely care about?
Article Summary: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple Inc. in 1976 alongside Steve Wozniak and helped transform the way people interacted with personal technology. The quote offers several ideas that extend beyond the words. Jobs’ life and career had its ups and downs; he faced difficulties, controversies, doubts and even opposition to his ideas.

Article Title: Is generative AI making us dumber?
Article Text:
Is AI impacting our creativity ?

We think AI is writing for us, but it is actually thinking for us.(File Photo)

Nature Human Behaviour

Tracing the origins of original thinking

What can AI never teach you

Art of

Creative Writing

How to protect creativity while outsourcing it

As creative professionals are increasingly using AI to execute their ideas, where are they drawing the line when each response carries the temptation of lightening the burden further?(File Photo)

Shatak: Sangh Ke 100 Varsh

How to ensure that your work isn’t AI slop

How to beat the blank page?

Rather than trying to take leaps, we can begin with a single step: filling a blank sheet every day.(File Photo)

Are you stuck in this rut? You sit with the noble intention of creation, armed with your drink and a cloud of thoughts. Ten minutes later, the cup is empty, and so is the page. Your creative process is an exercise in staring at the void, struggling to determine how your thoughts will precipitate, and eventually doomscrolling to escape the question: were you ever creative in the first place? Suddenly, you grab your device and search for your saviour among the three musketeers: ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. You select the worthiest, convert your cloud of thoughts into a droplet for a prompt and are promptly served a buffet of your thoughts, turned into purple prose. You make a few edits, such as removing the em dashes and the “it’s not x, it’s y” phrases, and proudly claim the work as your own.While you have been rescued from the torment of self-deprecation, you are left with a more unsettling question: if you are always spared the struggle of creating, are you gradually surrendering the originality that drives it?On the surface, AI is just a tool helping us articulate our thoughts, but slowly and steadily, it is robbing us of our latent creative spark. If we think about the nature of AI-assisted creative content and compare it with other AI-assisted content, we arrive at a startling conclusion: AI not only writes for us, but thinks for us as well. This is evident in the subtle uniformity of the content thus developed. The similarity in the structure and nature of the content strikes you. In a study published in, five experiments were conducted in which participants tackled challenges such as designing a toy from a paper bag, a brick and a fan.They either worked without technology or used ChatGPT or Google. Their final ideas were rated for originality and appropriateness, including usefulness, which together formed the study’s creativity score. On average, ChatGPT-assisted ideas scored the highest, suggesting that ChatGPT could connect distantly related ideas and express them coherently.However, this research missed an important criterion that would expose the true impact of using AI in the creative process.Researchers from Wharton reanalysed the data from this research. Rather than assessing each idea in isolation, they assessed how different each idea was from the others. This led to the discovery of a previously overlooked pattern: the concepts behind ChatGPT-assisted ideas were less diverse. The sharpest example came from the task of asking participants to design a toy for a seven-year-old using a paper bag, a brick and a fan. One hundred per cent of the unaided human ideas were classified as unique, compared with only 41.2% of the human ideas developed with ChatGPT and only 6% of the outputs generated entirely by ChatGPT. It was also reported that nine participants using ChatGPT independently arrived at the same name: “Build-a-Breeze Castle.” This revealed that AI raised the quality of an individual idea while narrowing the range of ideas from which it emerged.To prevent our work from ending up in the landfill of “AI slop”, we must learn to express our creativity independently.To understand why our creativity is so vulnerable to external influences such as AI, we need to trace it back to its origins. Debraj Mookerjee, an Associate Professor of English at Ramjas College, University of Delhi, traces this to one of the first creative activities most people encounter. He says, “There’s a kind of a parametric approach to learning, and it starts with the drawing class. Your primary goal is to not allow your paint to cross the line. If there’s an outline for a mountain or a sky or a face, the teacher will upbraid you for your paint going beyond that line.” He believes that it symbolises something much larger. “It’s very symbolic of the kind of restraint that is imposed on thinking in young students, because I believe that we actually train our students to be consumers of knowledge and not producers of knowledge,” he asserts. He argues that instead of imposing restrictions, institutions must equip students with “the ability to validate your own thoughts”, as the courage to think originally comes from a certain sense of freedom.If you are given the freedom to think originally, can you ensure that you are thinking independently? The key is to use a precious, inexpensive resource that is far better than your next scroll or prompt: your experience of being human. Ramesh Menon, who has conducted several creative-writing workshops as part of the Sri Aurobindo Centre for Arts and Creativity and has authored, designs exercises that remove students from the world of screens and return them to their senses. One of his in-person workshops begins by taking away the sense on which people arguably depend the most: sight.He explains, “The idea is to use all your senses. As you walk on the ground, which area is hot, which area is cold, where is the sun? Where is the shade? How rough is the bark of the tree? What are different leaves like? The smell of wet mud, the feel of the grass as you lie down on it.” Apart from taking away a sense, he also gives his students music as a sensory prompt: they listen to it and begin writing as soon as it stops. He believes that AI can never compete with the inspiration you derive from your own sensory experiences. To encourage this, he takes his students on an excursion to Lodhi Garden and gives them an interesting assignment to complete there: “Imagine you are ghosts from 450 years ago. Write your autobiography. What was that era like? What were the kind of experiences you went through and how did you die? They sit there and write everything in three hours.” Along with this, he has set a golden rule for his workshops: no AI.Today, creative professionals are increasingly using AI to execute their ideas and work within the practical constraints of time, scale and budget. But where does one draw the line when each response carries the temptation of lightening the burden further? Aashish Mall , director of, which has been described as India’s first full-length AI feature film, draws a firm boundary between ideation and AI-assisted execution. “Every emotional beat gets written on paper, offline, before I open any AI tool,” he says. He expresses concern about how AI’s ability to produce spectacular images can shift a filmmaker’s attention from “what should we show?” to “what can we show?” He understood this while creating a scene in which a ten-year-old loses both his parents to the plague and realised: “Although the AI render was technically beautiful, a rendered face cannot carry a loss like that. ” With this realisation, he used a song by Shankar Mahadevan, which he believed “added the human element the render couldn’t reach.” The experience reinforced the importance of maintaining boundaries in his execution: “AI is fluent in surfaces. Interiority belongs to us.”A machine may generate the shot, but, as Mall puts it, “only a human can make it mean something.” He emphasises the importance of fiercely protecting the ability to comprehend the Ws: “Who you are, what you care about, when your moment is, where you belong, why you’re making anything at all—these are the constants. You can adapt to technology for the H, how you execute. It will keep changing, so let it.”While you have learned about the origin, development and balanced outsourcing of the creative process, how can you ensure that you have complete creative control over your AI-assisted output? Tanmay Gaur, a second-generation, multi-speciality filmmaker and media producer who has used generative AI across several productions, believes that the key is to shift the focus from what AI can generate to what a creator chooses to keep by relying on their own taste. He says, “Taste has always been a very individualistic concept, as all kinds of media you consume is what gives you your taste.” He also mentions the role of personal experiences and beliefs in developing taste, saying, “Your own ideologies, your own philosophies will give you your taste.” He argues that AI’s most valuable use lies in creative execution rather than judgement. “It’s not really a tool that gives you taste, a tool is just a way to create as per your taste.” Through this understanding, you can protect the originality of your ideation and execution without being influenced by AI.Developing our creativity in a world that loves to dictate, judge and impose is certainly not easy. Rather than trying to take leaps, we can start with a single step: filling a blank sheet every day using “stream-of-consciousness writing”, a technique in which you record your thoughts exactly as they occur, bypassing your internal editor, grammar and structure. This will help us get rid of our inhibitions. We can then proceed to work on our creative assignments, challenging ourselves with various prompts. Pushing through the tedium we experience before finding our creative spark and flow is important, as that is when we are strongly tempted to take shortcuts. Once we learn how to deal with this, along with the confusion and chaos of the creative process, we must face one of our biggest fears: presenting our imperfect original work for feedback. We can exercise our power to filter this feedback, separating constructive criticism from mere trolling, and act upon it accordingly. It is only after this that we can indulge in creating naturally without depending on anything artificial for ideation.So, before you try to escape the tedium, think about the child who embraced the creative process independently, and try to honour that child in you by enduring the process for a little longer.
Article Summary: We think AI is writing for us, but it is actually thinking for us. To prevent our work from ending up in the landfill of ‘AI slop’, we must learn to express our creativity independently. To understand why our creativity is vulnerable to external influences such as AI, we need to trace it back to its origins.

Article Title: Google DeepMind shuts down Nobel Prize-winning AI systems team AlphaFold; as VP Research says: Our strategy over the last nine years has been to …
Article Text:
Google DeepMind shifting priorities

Top Google DeepMind executive says ‘strategy has evolved’



Google has seen some high-profile exits to competitors in recent months



Google DeepMind has dismantled the research team behind AlphaFold, its Nobel Prize-winning AI system that has been designed for predicting protein structures. The restructuring marks a major strategic shift for the laboratory as it realigns its focus toward large language models (LLMs) and general scientific automation.According to an analysis of recent job moves and company insiders undertaken by The Financial Times, the majority of the original AlphaFold paper authors have been reassigned internally or departed the company. Almost a quarter of the full-time DeepMind authors who built the original AlphaFold papers have left Google altogether, the report said.Google DeepMind confirmed to the publication that remaining researchers have transitioned to other internal initiatives, including projects built around Google's flagship Gemini model, nuclear fusion, genomics and enzyme design while others moved to Alphabet's commercial drug-discovery spin-off, Isomorphic Labs.The dissolution of the AlphaFold unit points to how the rise of LLMs has reshaped priorities across top AI laboratories. Pushmeet Kohli, vice president of research at Google DeepMind and head of its AI for Science team, explained that the lab is moving away from assembling isolated teams around single, long-term scientific targets.“Our strategy over the last nine years has been to focus on grand challenges... a concrete goal every project is focused on.The strategy has evolved,” Kohli said.Instead of focusing on standalone problems like protein folding, DeepMind is reportedly prioritising Gemini-powered systems capable of assisting scientists across various fields and eventually automating parts of the research process, while competing directly with rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic.Launched in 2018, AlphaFold revolutionised biological research by solving a 50-year-old challenge in structural biology. The accomplishment earned DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis and vice president/engineering fellow John Jumper the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2024. However, key leaders behind the project have recently departed:Jumper, co-recipient of the 2024 Nobel Prize, recently left DeepMind to join competitor Anthropic. Core AlphaFold researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel have also exited and joined Anthropic.
Article Summary: Majority of original AlphaFold paper authors have been reassigned internally or departed the company. Almost a quarter of the full-time DeepMind authors have left Google altogether. The restructuring marks a major strategic shift for the laboratory as it realigns its focus toward large language models (LLMs)

Article Text:

A bunch of companies across the industry are trying to figure out and get those workflows right so that you're not just AI native from code development, but you're AI native in how you actually operate,”

DoorDash says AI writes most of its code, but workflows remain unchanged

Other tech executives who have also highlighted AI's limitations

"vibe coding"

"Sometimes I get a little bit of a heart attack because it's not like super amazing code necessarily all the time. It's very bloaty, and there's a lot of copy-paste, and there's awkward abstractions that are brittle, and it works, but it's just really gross,”

DoorDash CEO Tony Xu has challenged a common belief related to artificial intelligence (AI). Xu believes AI cannot dramatically improve software engineers' productivity through coding alone because writing code accounts for only a portion of an engineer's workday. According to a report by Business Insider, speaking on an episode of the Uncapped podcast released this week, Xu said,He added that engineers spend much of their time on product reviews, design discussions, and cross-functional collaboration, areas where AI workflows also need improvement.Xu's remarks contrast with statements made by several technology executives who have highlighted AI's impact on software engineering productivity. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said AI coding assistants have significantly improved productivity and could automate much of programming, allowing engineers to focus on higher-level work. During the company's May earnings call, he said AI-generated code has become common inside the organisation, but that has not yet translated into structural changes.he added.According to Xu, AI-assisted coding is only one part of a broader productivity equation, with collaboration, planning and decision-making still requiring significant human involvement.Xu is among a smaller group of executives who have publicly discussed the limits of current AI tools. Earlier this month, Wix CEO Avishai Abrahami said the technology industry may be overstating AI's capabilities while discussing the company's acquisition of vibe-coding platform Base44.Abrahami said.Former Tesla AI head and OpenAI founding member Andrej Karpathy, who coined the term, has also acknowledged limitations in AI-generated software.he said.

Article Title: Why Microsoft is asking Google and Amazon, two of its biggest Cloud rivals, for 'help' despite spending $190 billion on AI
Article Text:
Microsoft's $190 billion AI spend still isn't buying it enough computing power—it is now shopping at Amazon and Google

Microsoft is building data centres as fast as it can, and AI demand is still outrunning them

Copilot first, R&D second, Azure customers with whatever is left: Microsoft's CFO has already said it out loud

Inside Microsoft, the compute queue is causing arguments executives can't settle

Microsoft sells computing capacity to the world. This year, it is buying some. The company is spending a record $190 billion to build AI infrastructure, and it is still short enough on servers that it has started evaluating Amazon and Google—its two biggest cloud rivals—as suppliers.According to a Business Insider report, the company is now evaluating Amazon and Google as sources of additional cloud capacity, with one person familiar with the discussions putting it plainly: "We are shopping for capacity everywhere." Amazon has already stepped in once, bailing Microsoft out following a series of GitHub outages this year. Microsoft also explored leasing infrastructure from Oracle but walked away over security and compliance concerns. For a company whose Azure pitch rests on owning the stack end to end, that is an uncomfortable place to be.The shortage is not for want of money. Microsoft's capital expenditure this year is largely going into data-centre capacity for AI workloads, and executives told Business Insider the company is still constrained. Demand for computing infrastructure has simply outpaced how fast Microsoft can build. Azure remains its fastest-growing strategic business, but internally it has turned into a balancing act over where finite GPUs actually go.Curiously, the crunch has not slowed the sales side. Microsoft is raising quotas for Azure salespeople, some by as much as 30% this year, according to people familiar with the change.Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood explained the pecking order on the company's January earnings call. Microsoft solves first for rising usage in sales and the accelerating pace of M365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot, its first-party apps. Then it invests in long-term R&D and product innovation. Whatever is left over goes to Azure customers, whose demand keeps climbing regardless.The numbers behind that choice are small but telling. Hood said that if Microsoft had pushed the GPUs that came online in the first half of its fiscal year to Azure instead of its own AI products, Azure growth would have crossed 40% rather than landing at 39%. Microsoft reported $75 billion in Azure revenue for its 2025 fiscal year. Investors were not soothed. That earnings report set off a post-earnings decline of more than 10%, with the market questioning a softer Azure outlook against record AI spending.Executives who spoke to Business Insider said those tradeoffs have only sharpened since.The rationing has produced friction that is now spilling out internally. "All of the supply is gone once you solve for frontier labs and our internal businesses like M365 and Microsoft AI," one executive told Business Insider.Another framed the frustration as a question nobody has a clean answer to: "Why would Satya prioritize growing Adobe over growing M365?" The same person added, "I have no idea how we're going to land that message with customers."That is the harder problem. Microsoft can buy capacity from Amazon and Google if it has to. What it cannot easily buy is a story its salespeople can tell enterprise customers about why their workloads are behind OpenAI's and behind Copilot's in the queue.Investors get a fresh read on Wednesday, when Microsoft reports fourth-quarter results. Azure's growth rate and any update on capacity constraints will matter more than usual, with the stock already down more than 24% from 12 months ago.
Article Summary: Microsoft is spending a record $190 billion to build AI infrastructure. The company is still short enough on servers that it has started evaluating Amazon and Google. The shortage is not for want of money. Demand for computing infrastructure has simply outpaced how fast Microsoft can build.

Article Title: Anthropic's Claude code creator Boris Cherny has an important tip for Claude users that's an evergreen leadership lesson: Stop telling Claude how to...
Article Text:
Boris Cherny, creator of Anthropic's Claude Code, says most users are over-instructing their AI

Why Claude Code creator says over-specifying every step is the most common Claude prompting mistake right now

AI chatbot prompting tips age fast, and Boris Cherny says what worked six months ago may be working against you now

Beyond prompting: Cherny's take on how companies should actually measure AI returns

The most common mistake Boris Cherny sees from Claude users isn't a bad prompt. It's too much prompt. Speaking at a Y Combinator event on Saturday, the creator of Anthropic's Claude Code said people routinely hand the model a numbered march order—do this, then this, then this—and then wonder why the result feels boxed in. His diagnosis is blunt: that style of instruction is a leftover habit, and today's models don't need it.What he recommends instead reads like something out of a management handbook, and that's roughly the point. Describe the task. Set the guardrails. Say clearly what a finished job looks like. Then get out of the way. "Then just go let the model cook and come back in a little bit," Cherny said, adding that the output tends to surprise people who try it.Cherny's argument is that users are underestimating the size of the task a modern model can take on. When someone dictates the method as well as the outcome, they're spending their prompt on the part the model is already good at figuring out, and spending none of it on the part that actually matters—what success looks like. Be specific about the destination, he says, and loose about the route.Cherny was candid that this approach has a shelf life attached to it in both directions.His own advice, he said, probably wouldn't have held up six months ago. The models weren't there yet. That makes prompting less a fixed skill than a moving one, where the techniques people carefully learned in 2025 quietly become friction in 2026.He isn't alone in the read. Google Brain cofounder Andrew Ng made a similar case last year under the label "lazy prompting"—the idea being that detail gets added to a prompt only at the point where it's actually required, not pre-emptively.The advice lands alongside a separate framework Cherny laid out in a series of X posts earlier this month, aimed at enterprises trying to justify their AI bills. Usage dashboards are worth watching, he wrote, but they track activity rather than return. The sharper question is whether the company would have put engineering hours into that task anyway—and what those hours would have cost. The larger gain, he added, arrives once fixing and maintaining runs quietly in the background and teams move on to work that wasn't feasible before.That's the mood across the industry now. The token-burn arms race of early 2026 has cooled, with Jamie Dimon and Sam Altman both flagging cost-versus-value as the question of the moment. Cherny reckons dozens, possibly hundreds, of useful model capabilities are still undiscovered—but you only stumble into them if you stop dictating the route.
Article Summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Anthropic's Claude Code, says most users are over- instructing their AI. He says people routinely hand the model a numbered march order. Cherny reckons dozens, possibly hundreds, of useful model capabilities are still undiscovered.

Article Title: Sam Altman has a message for Meta creating AI version of CEO Mark Zuckerberg: People don't really want an AI CEO, I think the world wants to know about ...
Article Text:
Meta creating AI version of CEO Mark Zuckerberg



Shift in thinking



Human judgment still matters



OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has a message for Meta as its experiments with building an AI version of CEO Mark Zuckerberg: people don’t want an artificial intelligence running a company. “I think the world wants to know about the person that’s going to be responsible for the decisions of a company, and who they’re going to hold accountable if they make bad ones, and they don’t really want an AI CEO,” Altman said on the Invest Like The Best podcast this week, as reported by Business Insider. His remarks come days after reports that Meta is developing an AI-powered version of Zuckerberg to assist employees — a project described by the Times of India as an effort to create “more than one Mark Zuckerberg” inside the company .Recently, it was reported by Facebook-parent Meta is creating the AI version of its CEO Mark Zuckerberg. As reported by Financial Times, the project is part of Meta’s broader push to embed AI deeply into its products and operations. The FT report suggests that the company is working on photorealistic, 3D AI characters capable of real-time interaction. While Meta has experimented with celebrity-inspired chatbots and user-generated AI personas, insiders say the focus has now shifted to building a Zuckerberg character trained on his mannerisms, tone, and public statements.This goal of the company will enable the employees to feel more connected to the founder, even when he is not present physically.Mark Zuckerberg is personally involved in the training and testing of his AI version. As per the report he has been spending around five to ten hours a week coding on AI projects and is also attending technical reviews. This effort of Zuckerberg is separate from his ‘CEO agent’ project, which is made to support him by retrieving information quickly.Altman’s stance marks a shift from last November, when he told the Conversations with Tyler podcast that it would be a failure if OpenAI wasn’t the first major company to be run by an AI CEO. Now, he says the focus on humanity explains why AI hasn’t “upended” the economy as quickly as he once predicted. “People have a great degree of trust and enjoyment in working with other people,” Altman said, adding that most still prefer human consultants, sales reps, and engineers over AI counterparts.Altman argued that even as AI models produce spectacular results, people value the human element behind art, literature, and leadership. “You read a novel, you want to know about the person behind it,” he said. He suggested the world may need a new word to capture the kind of judgment humans excel at — something AI continues to struggle with.
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says people don’t want an artificial intelligence running a company. His remarks come days after reports that Meta is developing an AI- powered version of Zuckerberg to assist employees. Altman argued that even as AI models produce spectacular results, people value the human element behind art, literature, and leadership.

Article Title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon on being fired from Citigroup; says: I was summoned to a meeting with Sandy Weill and John Reed and asked to resign due to ...
Article Text:
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon shares two life-changing incidents in an interview

Jamie Dimon on unexpected Citigroup exit



Jamie Dimon on March 2020 heart emergency



JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon recently reflected on two of the most defining crises of his life and career during an appearance on The Master Investor Podcast. The first is his sudden firing from Citigroup in 1998 and, the second, a near-fatal heart emergency in 2020. The veteran Wall Street executive opened up about how a high-profile corporate setback reshaped his career path and how facing mortality left him at peace with his life and legacy.Jamie Dimon recalled his 1998 termination as president of Citigroup as a turning point in his career. After playing a major role in building the financial giant alongside his mentor, Sandy Weill, Dimon was unexpectedly summoned to a meeting with Weill and co-CEO John Reed.“I was summoned to a meeting with Sandy Weill and John Reed and asked to resign due to organisational changes,” Jamie Dimon shared. As per a report by Benzinga, the sudden request left Dimon initially baffled. Upon returning home to share the news, his youngest daughter asked if the family would now have to “sleep on the streets”.Despite the public nature of the dismissal, Dimon emphasised that he refused to let the event compromise his identity.He said that the firing “affected my net worth, not my self-worth.” Shortly after his exit, around 50 senior Citibank managers gathered at his apartment to bid him farewell.Dimon briefly considered walking away from Wall Street after a 1999 conversation with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos , but ultimately decided to remain in finance.In 2000, Dimon invested $60 million—roughly half his net worth at the time—into Bank One, a bold move that set the stage for Bank One’s eventual merger with JPMorgan Chase, where he became CEO.Beyond corporate battles, Jamie Dimon recounted the emergency open-heart surgery he underwent in March 2020 to repair an aortic dissection, which is a life-threatening tear in the heart's main artery. Recognizing the severity of the condition, Dimon knew immediately that the odds were stacked against him.“I knew at that point in time that you know there might be goodbye. I told my wife, call the company and tell them exactly what’s happening so they can do what they got to do,” Dimon recalled. Jamie Dimon shared that the near-death experience brought a sense of peace, reflecting that while he had made mistakes throughout his career.

Article Title: As Nasa’s Moon to Mars mission nears, scientists may finally have an answer to the problem that would have killed anyone standing on the Moon in 1972
Article Text:
FILE - In this April 11, 1970, photo made available by NASA, the Saturn V rocket carrying the crew of the Apollo 13 mission to the moon launches from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. (NASA via AP)

Why permanent magnet radiation shielding beats superconducting magnets on a spacecraft

Deep space radiation protection has barely moved since Apollo, and Artemis II proves it

In August 1972, in the gap between Apollo 16 and Apollo 17, the Sun let loose a burst of particles severe enough that Nasa later described it as a near-miss. Nobody was out there to catch it. Had a crew been on the lunar surface or in transit, the dose would have been fatal. That single event has hung over every deep-space mission plan since.A research team from Italy and Germany now says it has a partial fix, and it does not run on cryogenics or reactor-grade power. It runs on permanent magnets. The team packed 1,482 neodymium-iron-boron magnets, each about 1.6 square inches, into an 11-square-foot array weighing 661 pounds. In testing, the array deflected roughly 20% of solar particles in the 0.1 to 10 megaelectronvolt range. High-energy particles still punched through, so this is not a force field. It is a first layer.Cosmic radiation is mostly protons moving very fast. When a charged particle crosses a magnetic field, the Lorentz force acts on it at right angles to both the field and its path, nudging it off course. Scale that up and you bend particles away from the crew module.Earlier work chased the same idea with superconducting magnets generating a 1-tesla field. Those need cryogenic cooling and power that never fails, two things spacecraft struggle to promise. Permanent magnets ask for neither. The catch is deployment. Cosmic rays arrive from every direction, so the magnets would need to wrap most of the hull, and protons striking the magnets themselves can throw off secondary radiation.Leaving Earth means crossing the Van Allen belts, two rings of high-energy particles held in place by the planet's magnetic field. Beyond that, galactic cosmic rays and solar flares are constant. The lunar surface itself carries two to three times the radiation seen aboard the ISS.Apollo 14 astronauts absorbed about 1.14 rads across their mission, roughly double an abdominal CT scan. Survivable, and that is the trap. Those crews simply never met a major solar particle event.The current contingency is not much better. Artemis II astronauts had one option if a flare erupted mid-flight: stack cargo and supplies into a makeshift fort and wait it out. A hybrid system built around passive magnets would at least replace the cardboard fortress with something engineered.
Article Summary: Team packed 1,482 neodymium-iron-boron magnets, each about 1.6 square inches, into an 11-square-foot array weighing 661 pounds. In testing, the array deflected roughly 20% of solar particles in the 0.1 to 10 megaelectronvolt range.

Article Title: Anthropic's Claude Mythos ‘breaks’ AES encryption that protects the entire internet; including online bank transactions, online chats and more
Article Text:
Claude Mythos broke a weakened AES; 800 times faster than any human method

Why cracking a "reduced-round" cipher still matters to anyone with a banking app

Anthropic’s model refused the job first, then burned a billion tokens finishing it

What the findings signal for NIST standards, the quantum race and AI safety rules

Anthropic says its most powerful AI model has found new mathematical weaknesses in the encryption that holds the internet together. Claude Mythos Preview, a model still not available to the public, worked out an improved way to attack a stripped-down version of AES, the cipher sitting underneath online bank transfers, encrypted chats, Wi-Fi networks and stored data. The company published the findings on Tuesday alongside two research papers.Nothing you use today is broken. Mythos attacked a 7-round variant of AES-128, which normally runs 10 rounds, and its method is 200 to 800 times faster than the previous best. The second finding bites harder. Mythos halved the effective key strength of HAWK, a post-quantum signature scheme shortlisted by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology, after HAWK had already survived two years and two rounds of expert human review. It took the model 60 hours. Anthropic shared both results with US government and industry partners before publishing.Cryptographers routinely weaken algorithms on purpose to see where the cracks might appear later. Think of it as solving an easier version of a hard maths problem to spot the pattern. The AES attack also assumes an attacker can request 2¹⁰⁵ chosen encryptions, which is not happening on any machine that exists.AES was adopted in 2001 and is believed to have roughly as many possible keys as there are atoms in the observable universe.The point is the trajectory, not the damage. Anthropic researcher Nicholas Carlini, who previously worked at Google, said of last year's models: "They could not do problems that I could do when I was 16."The discovery process is the strangest part of the story. Claude initially declined to work on AES because it was convinced no improvement was possible, telling researchers there was nothing easy left to find in the most-studied block cipher around. A researcher nudged it with a typo-riddled prompt noting that models assume the task is impossible and so never try. Claude then rewrote its own agent harness to hunt for novel ideas.Over the next three days it produced several hundred million tokens and landed on a technique it named the Möbius Bridge, a fingerprinting method that removes one of the 2⁵⁶ guesses an attacker previously had to make. By the end it had output about a billion tokens. Each of the two results cost roughly $100,000 in API spend. Two Anthropic researchers, neither a cryptography expert, then spent close to a month confirming the maths held up.For HAWK, the practical fallout is immediate. The expected cost of recovering a HAWK-256 key drops from 2⁶⁴ to 2³⁸, and doubling key sizes to compensate strips away much of what made the scheme attractive.Anthropic also flagged a working attack on 13-round LEA that recovers a key in under an hour on a desktop, plus smaller gains against Serpent-128, Salsa20 and SHA-1. It has released CryptanalysisBench, built with ETH Zurich, Tel Aviv University and the University of Haifa, to track how fast this capability grows.Mythos remains restricted. When it launched in April, Anthropic limited access to select government agencies after the model proved unusually good at finding and exploiting software bugs. Glenn Gerstell, former general counsel at the NSA, questioned whether anyone should feel comfortable assuming strong encryption stays safe two years out.
Article Summary: Anthropic says its most powerful AI model has found new mathematical weaknesses in the encryption that holds the internet together. Claude Mythos Preview worked out an improved way to attack a stripped-down version of AES, the cipher sitting underneath online bank transfers, encrypted chats, Wi-Fi networks and stored data.

Article Title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX drops nearly 50% in one month as $1.5 trillion wiped out; experts warn ‘crazier’ next week
Article Text:
Elon Musk-owned SpaceX's share drop nearly 50% since its peak

What is options pricing

Current stock price: If the stock price moves closer to or beyond the option's strike price, the option usually becomes more valuable.

Strike price: The fixed price at which the stock can be bought or sold.

Time until expiration: More time usually means a higher option price because there's a greater chance the stock price will move in the buyer's favour.

Volatility: Stocks that move up and down more sharply tend to have more expensive options because they offer a greater chance of large gains.

Interest rates and dividends: These can also affect an option's value, though usually to a smaller extent.

Elon Musk-led SpaceX and Tesla have erased a combined $1.5 trillion in market capitalization since mid-June. As per a report by CNBC, the decline follows an almost 50% drop in SpaceX’s valuation since its recent peak. Additionally, Tesla shares have fallen by 18% since the company’s earnings report last week. But this does not end here. The CNBC report warns that it “might get even crazier next week, based on options pricing around SpaceX’s earnings report”. According to the report, options prices indicate a 15% swing in SpaceX with implied volatility of 122 in the stock – higher than every company in the S&P 500 other than SanDisk.The earnings release also triggers the company's special lock-up period, allowing insiders to sell shares before the usual 180-day limit. It is speculated that more than 900 million shares, representing about 20% of the locked-up stock, will become eligible for trading.“The early lockup two days after earnings presents a tricky setup for options traders, who can usually count on a stock’s implied volatility falling after earnings.Earnings present predictable risk for stockholders who often have to hedge their positions, and once that risk passes — even if the stock crashes, volatility usually declines,” the report said.Options pricing is the process of determining how much an options contract is worth. An option is a financial contract that gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a stock at a fixed price before a certain date. The price one pays for an option is called the premium. This premium is determined by several factors:
